authorization: Owner approved the continuation recommendations and asked for paper-style subcluster UMAP and trajectory-analogous figures for CD177 and reversible state conversion
exposure: FULL. Every endpoint of batch1 and the continuation (EN0-EN7) has been evaluated and reported in RESULTS_CONTINUATION.md. This contract is an openly exploratory follow-up on exposed data; it is not preregistration and cannot yield independent validation.
inherited_rules: Gates, modules, inclusion rules, 30-cell floor, 10-per-side bin floor, library units, mapped-gene denominators and EN7_library_CPM_v1 are inherited unchanged from the continuation contract unless named below.

paper_pipeline_as_documented.source: England et al. 2025 STAR Methods, read 2026-09-28
paper_pipeline_as_documented.qc: >15% mitochondrial, <1000 detected genes, >50,000 UMIs removed; mitochondrial genes and genes in <3 cells dropped before normalization
paper_pipeline_as_documented.round1: log-normalize + scale, top 5,000 HVG, PCA, Louvain graph clustering, UMAP on first two dimensions; clusters of unwanted types discarded on Ptprc (immune), Pecam1 (endothelial), Col1a1 (mesenchymal), Foxj1 (ciliated) plus canonical markers
paper_pipeline_as_documented.round2: filtered objects integrated, counts renormalized, PCA / clustering / UMAP repeated; clusters annotated by known markers and by comparison with published regeneration states
paper_pipeline_as_documented.trajectory_method: NONE. The paper reports no pseudotime, RNA-velocity, Monocle, PAGA or similar analysis. Its reversible-transition claim rests on CD177/Itga2 double-positive immunofluorescence, organoid cultures from sorted states, orthotopic transplantation and EdU, plus the absence of a clone-size-versus-composition correlation.
paper_pipeline_as_documented.velocity_feasibility: RNA velocity is impossible on this deposit: GEO supplies CellRanger filtered count matrices only, with no spliced/unspliced layers or velocyto output.

FU_A_depth_control.question: Do the CD177 secondary associations (priming, AT2/AT1 identity, Itga2, shared/lesion modules) survive depth control?
FU_A_depth_control.population: transition-gated, primary-included cells in the two eligible libraries GSM7890835 and GSM7890836
methods_all_prespecified: within-transition thinning to a common budget of 3000 UMIs (seed 20260930), cells below the budget excluded and counted; gates and Cd177 grouping recomputed on the thinned counts
rank-based endpoint: within-library rank of each per-cell score, difference of mean ranks expressed as a rank-biserial correlation

detection-covariate residual: per-cell score residualized on log10(total UMIs) and on the number of detected genes by ordinary least squares within library, then the standardized mean difference recomputed on residuals
depth-decile stratified SMD: 10 equal-count depth bins, >=10 cells per side per bin, weights min(n_pos, n_neg)
FU_A_depth_control.decision_rule_frozen: An association is called depth-robust only if its direction is preserved in BOTH libraries under ALL FOUR methods AND the residualized |SMD| is at least half the unadjusted |SMD|. Otherwise it is reported as depth-dependent or inconclusive.
FU_A_depth_control.boundary: Depth control cannot remove ambient contamination or establish causality; Cd177 RNA is not surface protein.

FU_B_AT1_module_gate.question: Does an AT1 definition that is specific in an independently labelled dataset change the mixed-state readout?
FU_B_AT1_module_gate.new_gate: AT1_module_gate: mean log1p(CP10k) over Pdpn, Cav1, Aqp5, Spock2 (the AT1_identity module, disjoint from the Ager/Hopx/Clic5 detection gate) above a threshold
FU_B_AT1_module_gate.threshold_calibration: Fixed BEFORE application to England data as the value maximizing Youden's J for author_celltype == 'AT1' versus author_celltype == 'AT2' among Niethamer primary-included cells (25-sample atlas, all days). Recorded with its sensitivity and specificity.
FU_B_AT1_module_gate.application: Recompute the exclusive state rule with AT1_module_gate replacing the AT1 detection gate; recompute per-library composition, the mixed-state fraction and the Cd177 contrasts. Report both definitions side by side; the original gate is not deleted.
FU_B_AT1_module_gate.boundary: A threshold transferred across studies and chemistries is a descriptive harmonization, not a validated classifier.

FU_C_cluster_level_cd177.question: Is the CD177 association a property of the transition gate or of the Cd177-enriched cluster?
FU_C_cluster_level_cd177.population: Experiment-1 epithelial subclusters from FU_E round 2; the comparison is Cd177 >=1 UMI versus zero WITHIN each subcluster that meets the 30-cell floor on both sides
FU_C_cluster_level_cd177.endpoints: same primary (cycling) and secondary endpoints as EN5, same matched design
FU_C_cluster_level_cd177.boundary: Clusters are reconstruction-dependent; this is a sensitivity of the gate-based result, not an independent test.

FU_D_library_quality_model.question: How much of the between-library spread in response-high fraction is explained by technical quality?
FU_D_library_quality_model.outcome: fraction of primary-included cells above the frozen WT-baseline q90 response threshold (EN3 definition, unchanged)
FU_D_library_quality_model.predictors: median log10 UMIs, median detected genes, median mitochondrial percent, batch1 doublet fraction, immune-marker-high fraction
FU_D_library_quality_model.model: ordinary least squares, all five predictors entered together, no selection; report R-squared, coefficients and residuals by condition
FU_D_library_quality_model.boundary: 20 libraries and five predictors; descriptive variance accounting, not inference. Condition is confounded with library, so a high R-squared does not prove a technical origin.

FU_E_embedding_and_topology.question: Reproduce the paper's two-round epithelial subclustering and UMAP, and characterize state topology as far as the data allow
FU_E_embedding_and_topology.round1: per experiment, the continuation EN1 clustering already run (5,000 HVG, 30 PCs, 15 neighbours, igraph multilevel r 0.5/1.0/1.5, seed 20260928) is reused as round 1
FU_E_embedding_and_topology.contaminant_rule: a round-1 cluster at r = 1.0 is discarded when its detection fraction for any of Ptprc, Pecam1, Col1a1 or Foxj1 is >= 0.25 and its epithelial-anchor detection (>=2 of Epcam/Krt18/Krt19/Sftpc/Nkx2-1/Lamp3) is < 0.5; the rule is applied per experiment and its waterfall recorded
FU_E_embedding_and_topology.round2: retained cells renormalized, 5,000 HVG, 30 PCs, 15 neighbours, igraph multilevel r 0.5/1.0/1.5, seed 20260928; UMAP with min_dist 0.3, spread 1.0, seed 20260928, 2 components
FU_E_embedding_and_topology.annotation: clusters labelled by the frozen gates and modules plus the contaminant panels; no six-state target and no author-label equivalence claimed
topology: PAGA connectivity between round-2 clusters (scanpy default), reported as an undirected graph
diffusion pseudotime rooted at the cell with the highest AT2_identity score inside the largest AT2-gated cluster, reported as an ordering only
FU_E_embedding_and_topology.direction_boundary: PAGA connectivity and diffusion pseudotime are undirected descriptions of transcriptome similarity. They cannot establish a direction of travel, a transition rate, or bidirectional conversion. No arrow may be drawn on a figure from these quantities. RNA velocity is not computable on this deposit.
FU_E_embedding_and_topology.cd177_itga2_codetection: Within mutant RFP epithelial cells, count Cd177/Itga2 RNA co-detection at >=1 UMI each and compare with 200 permutations of the Itga2 indicator within depth-decile x cycling strata (seed 20260930). This is the RNA analogue of the paper's protein double-positive observation; RNA co-detection is not protein double positivity and does not demonstrate transition.

FU_T_transition_model_predictions.purpose: Test predictions that distinguish the paper's reversible-transition model from a forward reprogramming cascade, using RNA only. This tests consequences of the model; it does not measure transitions, directions or rates.
FU_T_transition_model_predictions.paper_model_as_read: England et al. 2025: mutant cells initially transform along a forward reprogramming pathway, then gain capacity for reversible transitions between DATP-like (Itga2), Cd177+ mixed and other mutant states, imparting equivalent proliferative potential on all mutant states. Evidence in the paper is CD177/Itga2 double-positive immunofluorescence, organoids and transplants from sorted states, EdU, and absence of a clone-size-versus-composition correlation.

T1_topology.prediction_reversible: round-2 mutant subclusters are mutually adjacent: PAGA connectivity is distributed across many pairs rather than concentrated in a chain
T1_topology.prediction_cascade: connectivity concentrated along a path, with low direct connectivity between non-adjacent states
T1_topology.readout: PAGA connectivity matrix between round-2 clusters restricted to mutant RFP epithelial cells; report the full matrix, the fraction of total connectivity carried by the largest spanning path, and the number of pairs above 0.1
T1_topology.boundary: undirected; a connected graph is compatible with rapid mixing AND with a continuum of states that never interconvert

T2_intermediate_density.prediction_reversible: cells occupy the transcriptional space between state centroids rather than only at them
T2_intermediate_density.readout: for each pair of round-2 mutant clusters, project cells onto the line joining the two centroids in the 30-PC space, bin into 10 equal-width bins, and report the density in the middle four bins relative to the two end bins (a filled-valley ratio). Report the same ratio after excluding cells flagged as doublets in batch1 and after depth-decile matching of the two clusters.
T2_intermediate_density.boundary: doublets, ambient RNA and depth all fill valleys; the ratio is descriptive and is reported alongside the doublet and depth sensitivities, never alone

T3_composition_stationarity.prediction_reversible: state composition approaches a stationary mix and changes little between later timepoints
T3_composition_stationarity.readout: per-library exclusive-state composition at Experiment-1 day 4 versus day 14 (mutant RFP) and Experiment-2 day 14 versus day 84 (Il1r1 heterozygous mutant RFP); report total variation distance between the mean compositions of each pair and the per-library range
T3_composition_stationarity.boundary: different timepoints are different mice, not longitudinal measurements; two timepoints per experiment cannot distinguish a stationary mix from a slow cascade, and this comparison is confounded with library and depth

T4_equipotency.prediction_reversible: cycling is comparable across mutant states (the model's functional core)
T4_equipotency.readout: within mutant RFP libraries, cycling score and the fraction with >=2 cycling markers per exclusive gate state and per round-2 cluster, with the 30-cell floor; depth-decile matched pairwise standardized mean differences between states; reported per library, never pooled across libraries
T4_equipotency.boundary: RNA cycling markers are not a proliferation assay and say nothing about long-term potential, which the paper measured with organoids, transplantation and EdU

not_computable_on_this_deposit: RNA velocity or any splicing-based direction: GEO supplies CellRanger filtered matrices with no spliced/unspliced layers; the only route is re-quantifying the 68 ENA runs, which requires remote compute and separate authorization
transition rates or detailed-balance tests: state occupancy over time does not identify a rate matrix, and timepoints are different animals
optimal-transport couplings between timepoints: the method imposes the time direction it would be asked to test, so it adds assumptions without discriminating power here; deliberately excluded
CellRank or any directed Markov chain built on a pseudotime or similarity kernel: its arrows follow from the kernel and root choice, not from the data; deliberately excluded
assignment of any cell to a founder class, or of any state to a position in a lineage
FU_T_transition_model_predictions.reporting_rule: Each prediction is reported as consistent, inconsistent or uninformative with respect to the two competing descriptions, with the confound that could produce the same pattern named in the same sentence. The word 'reversible' may not be applied to any quantity computed here.

FU_S_simulator_refit.question: Does a boundary-correct implementation change the fitted two-population parameters and their support relative to the literal script?
FU_S_simulator_refit.data: batch1 mouse-level clone sizes, support n >= 2, mutant RFP cohorts kras1w/kras2w/kras4w
FU_S_simulator_refit.implementations: literal and boundary-correct Gillespie from EN6, unchanged
FU_S_simulator_refit.fitting: simulated-likelihood on a fixed grid: fs in {0.04,0.08,0.12,0.16,0.20}, sigma_f in {2,4,6,8,10,12,14}/7 x 2, sigma_s in {0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}/7 x 2, r = q in {0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8}; 20 replicates x 2000 clones per grid point, seed 20260930; score = mean per-mouse multinomial log likelihood of the binned size distribution (bins 2,3,4,5-6,7-10,11-20,21-50,51+) with leave-one-mouse-out held-out scoring
FU_S_simulator_refit.comparison: best grid point per implementation, its held-out score, and the batch1 shifted-negative-binomial held-out score on the same bins
FU_S_simulator_refit.boundary: A coarse grid is not a maximum-likelihood fit; merger and segmentation of imaged clones are not modelled; agreement with the published curves is not evidence that a particular implementation produced them.

figures.FU_F01: paper-style two-round epithelial UMAP per experiment with gate-state, Cd177 and Itga2 overlays
figures.FU_F02: CD177 depth-control panel: four methods x two libraries x endpoints, with the frozen decision rule marked
figures.FU_F03: state topology: PAGA connectivity graph and diffusion-pseudotime distributions by cluster, captioned as undirected
figures.FU_F04: AT1 module gate calibration on Niethamer and its effect on England mixed-state composition
figures.FU_F05: simulator refit: grid likelihood surface and held-out comparison

reporting: One appended section in RESULTS_CONTINUATION.md or a separate RESULTS_FOLLOWUP.md, with the depth-robustness verdict per endpoint and an explicit statement that no direction of state conversion is established.

FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.purpose: Reproduce, on the deposited pooled spatial pair profiles, the comparison the source makes between wild-type neighbour clone SIZE (Figures 5G-5J) and neighbour DIFFERENTIATION, the pro-Sftpc-negative fraction (Figures 6E-6F), placing both on a common relative scale with the homeostatic Confetti datasets as the non-oncogenic reference the source also uses, and quantifying the bin-occupancy limitation the source methods name.
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.exposure_disclosure: The slope computation below was run as scoping BEFORE this block was frozen, on 28 September 2026, and its direction was seen. It is therefore an openly exploratory extension, not a preregistered test. No threshold or decision rule was tuned after seeing it; the rule below fixes the reporting, not the outcome.
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.source_claim: England et al. 2025 report that wild-type AT2 proliferation scales with proximity to mutant clones (Fig 5) while loss of pro-Sftpc is independent of proximity (Fig 6). The owner's reading notes flag the mechanism behind these opposing behaviours as the study's stated limitation.
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.unit: distance bin within a deposited dataset; bins with >=10 pair rows and midpoint <=400 um
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.estimand: pair-row-weighted least-squares slope of the binned profile against bin midpoint, per 100 um, reported raw and relative to the distal level (weighted mean of the last two eligible bins)
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.comparison: oncogenic datasets (kras4d/1w/2w/4w) against homeostatic Confetti datasets (conf1w-conf72w), and size-slope against differentiation-slope within each dataset
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.reporting_rule: Report both slopes for every eligible dataset with its pair-row count. State in the same sentence as any contrast that these are pooled rows without mouse or clone identifiers, so no mouse-level effect, no significance and no causal reading is available, and that a neighbour clone may appear in several pair rows.
named_rivals: clone merger near large mutant lesions inflating apparent neighbour size at short distance
detection and segmentation bias in dense regions
differing clone-density and tissue-area normalisation between datasets
distance in Confetti tissue is clone-to-clone while in Red2Kras it is clone-to-mutant, so the reference is analogous, not matched
declining bin occupancy with distance, named in the source methods, so distal anchors rest on few pair rows and relative slopes are sensitive to them
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.boundary: This cannot establish that proximity causes wild-type growth, nor that differentiation is truly proximity-independent; an absent slope with wide uncertainty is not evidence of independence.
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.relationship_to_source: This is a reproduction of the source's own contrast, not an independent one. England et al. state the conclusion directly: loss of pro-Sftpc was independent of proximity to mutant clones up to 300 um resolution, in contrast to wild-type expansion, suggesting that alternate mechanisms control self-renewal versus differentiation. The contribution here is recoverability from the deposit, a common relative scale for the two readouts, the Confetti slope for both, and an explicit occupancy audit.
FU_W_growth_differentiation_decoupling.scale_fairness_amendment: Added 28 September 2026 after the percent-of-distal-level estimand was questioned: an unbounded count compared against a bounded fraction on a relative scale is not a fair comparison, because a bounded readout mechanically yields shallower relative slopes and could produce apparent decoupling on its own. Both readouts are therefore also reported on multiplicative scales with no ceiling, a log link for mean neighbour clone size and a logit link for the pro-Sftpc-negative fraction, and each context is compared against the homeostatic datasets on the same link. This addresses the scale artefact only; clone merger, bin occupancy and the absence of an animal unit are unaffected.
